CveFindings.Explanation:
[CVE-2026-40021](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4f7c-pmjv-c25w): Apache Log4net: Silent log event loss in XmlLayout and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J due to unescaped XML 1.0 forbidden characters

Severity: MEDIUM

Apache Log4net's  XmlLayout https://logging.apache.org/log4net/manual/configuration/layouts.html#layout-list  and  XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J https://logging.apache.org/log4net/manual/configuration/layouts.html#layout-list , in versions before 3.3.0, fail to sanitize characters forbidden by the  XML 1.0 specification https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#charsets  in MDC property keys and values, as well as the identity field that may carry attacker-influenced data. This causes an exception during serialization and the silent loss of the affected log event.

An attacker who can influence any of these fields can exploit this to suppress individual log records, impairing audit trails and detection of malicious activity.

Users are advised to upgrade to Apache Log4net 3.3.0, which fixes this issue.

Affected dependencies:
  - log4net:2.0.12 (packages.config:10); range < 3.3.0; patched 

Recommended fix: upgrade log4net to 3.3.0 or later.

CveFindings.Explanation:
[CVE-2024-21319](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-59j7-ghrg-fj52): Microsoft ASP.NET Core project templates vulnerable to denial of service

Severity: MEDIUM

A Denial of Service vulnerability exists in ASP.NET Core project templates which utilize JWT-based authentication tokens. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated client to consume arbitrarily large amounts of server memory, potentially triggering an out-of-memory condition on the server and making the server no longer able to respond to legitimate requests. 

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at  https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/290

### Mitigation factors

This impacts only .NET Core-based projects that were created using any version of project templates listed in affected software. 
Other project templates e.g., console applications, MAUI applications, Windows Forms or WPF applications, are not affected.

## Affected software

This impacts only .NET Core-based projects that were created using any version of the below project templates.

-	ASP.NET Core Web App (Model-View-Controller)
-	ASP.NET Core Web API
-	ASP.NET Core Web App (Razor Pages)
-	Blazor Server App
-	Blazor WebAssembly App

## Advisory FAQ

### How do I know if I am affected?

If you are you using project templates listed in affected software, you may be exposed to the vulnerability.

### How do I fix the issue?

#### For existing projects:
If you ever created any of these projects via the dotnet new command or via Visual Studio's File -> New Project gesture, and if you enabled federated authentication at project creation time, your project may be vulnerable. To remediate the vulnerability, use your package manager to update any references you may have to the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect, and Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens packages to their respective latest versions. 
- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer/) 
- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect/) 

If your project does not reference any of those three packages, you are not exposed to this vulnerability.

#### For new projects:
To remediate this issue please update to the latest SDK listed below. Simply installing the SDK update is not sufficient to remediate projects already-created / already-deployed projects which existed prior to this update being released.

* To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET 6.0 or .NET 7.0. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET  SDKs.
* If you are using one of the affected packages, please update to the patched version listed above.
* If you have .NET 6.0 or greater installed, you can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. You will see output like the following;

```
.NET Core SDK (reflecting any global.json):

 Version:   7.0.200
 Commit:    8473146e7d

Runtime Environment:

 OS Name:     Windows
 OS Version:  10.0.18363
 OS Platform: Windows
 RID:         win10-x64
 Base Path:   C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk\7.0.300\

Host (useful for support):

  Version: 76.0.5
  Commit:  8473146e7d

.NET Core SDKs installed:

  7.0.200 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk]

.NET Core runtimes installed:

  Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 7.0.5 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.AspNetCore.App]
  Microsoft.NETCore.App 7.0.5 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.NETCore.App]
  Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App 7.0.5 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App]

To install additional .NET Core runtimes or SDKs:
  https://aka.ms/dotnet-download
```

* If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.101 SDK (for Visual Studio 2022 v17.8) from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0.
* If you're using .NET 7.0, you should download and install .NET SDK 7.0.115 (for Visual Studio 2022 v17.4) from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/7.0.
* If you're using .NET 6.0, you should download and install .NET SDK 6.0.321 (for Visual Studio 2022 v17.2) from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/6.0.

.NET 6.0, .NET 7.0, .NET 8.0 updates are also available from Microsoft Update. To access this either type "Check for updates" in your Windows search, or open Settings, choose Update & Security and then click Check for Updates.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

## Other Information

If you have found a potential security issue in .NET 8.0 or .NET 7.0 or .NET 6.0, please email details to secure@microsoft.com. Reports may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Core & .NET 5 Bounty.   - System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt:5.6.0 (packages.config:97); range >= 7.0.0-preview, < 7.1.2; patched

Recommended fix: upgrade affected Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens and System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt packages from 5.6.0 to 5.7.0 or later, and verify the advisory applicability for this .NET Framework MVC deployment.

CveFindings.Name: Microsoft ASP.NET Core project templates vulnerable to denial of service

CweFindings.Explanation: GetSequenceIdFromSelectedDBSequence casts the SQL sequence result from Int64 to int without a range check at CatalogDBInitializer.cs:327. The sequence is declared AS bigint at dbo.catalog_hilo.Sequence.sql:5, so values above Int32.MaxValue can be truncated when assigned as catalog IDs.
CweFindings.Description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.
CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types

CweFindings.Explanation: The Index action accepts pageSize and pageIndex from query parameters without bounds and passes them through. CatalogService multiplies them for Skip and uses pageSize for Take; the view model divides by pageSize and casts the ceiling to int. Zero, negative, or extreme values can produce a divide-by-zero/overflow or incorrect pagination results.
CweFindings.Description: The product performs a calculation that generates incorrect or unintended results that are later used in security-critical decisions or resource management.
CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Calculation

CweFindings.Explanation: UpLoadImageFromFile opens a FileStream with File.OpenRead at line 111, uploads it at line 116, and exits without disposing the stream. Repeated catalog initialization can retain file handles and resources.
CweFindings.Description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.
CweFindings.Name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime

CweFindings.Explanation: UpLoadImageFromFile opens a file handle with File.OpenRead at line 111 and never closes or disposes it after UploadFromStream at line 116, so repeated calls can exhaust file handles.
CweFindings.Description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.
CweFindings.Name: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime

CweFindings.Explanation: The public Index action accepts an unbounded pageSize query parameter and passes it to CatalogService, which calls Take(pageSize).ToList() without a maximum. A very large pageSize can cause a large database result to be materialized in memory.
CweFindings.Description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.
CweFindings.Name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a SingleInstance. The singleton owns a mutable List<CatalogItem> shared across concurrent web requests.
CweFindings.Description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.
CweFindings.Name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context

CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogServiceMock mutates and reads its shared catalogItems list in create, update, and remove operations without synchronization. Concurrent requests can race while reading or modifying the list.
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.
CweFindings.Name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context

CweFindings.Explanation: The singleton mock catalog is shared across request threads, but its list operations are not protected by a lock or concurrent collection, allowing simultaneous access during writes and reads.
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.
CweFindings.Name: Improper Synchronization

CweFindings.Explanation: The shared mutable catalogItems list is accessed by request methods without synchronization. A lock exists in CatalogItemHiLoGenerator for a different resource, but it does not guard this list.
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
CweFindings.Name: Missing Synchronization

CweFindings.Explanation: The checked-in local Docker Compose override sets a literal SQL Server SA password for the database container and repeats it in the health-check command; the application connection string also uses the built-in SA credential. These are development credentials stored in plaintext configuration, not secret references.
CweFindings.Description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.
CweFindings.Name: Use of Hard-coded Password

CweFindings.Explanation: InitializeCatalogImages sets the entire pics blob container to BlobContainerPublicAccessType.Blob (public blob reads). The same container receives temporary user uploads via UploadTempImage, and the PicController upload action has no local authorization attribute, so uploaded temporary blobs are also publicly readable by URL.
CweFindings.Description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.
CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource

CweFindings.Explanation: The sign-in action logs only a generic entry message before challenging OpenID Connect. It does not record the authentication result or principal, so successful and failed authentication outcomes are not auditable from the application log.
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging

CweFindings.Explanation: The checked-in local Docker Compose override sets a literal SQL Server SA password for the database container and repeats it in the health-check command; the application connection string also uses the built-in SA credential. These are development credentials stored in plaintext configuration, not secret references.
CweFindings.Description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
CweFindings.Name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
